mainTopic: Honoring an אבל and רבא's ruling on collecting from heirs; the dispute over a daughter's money held by a שליש; and the start of אילפא's challenge
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of רב ענן's letter. מר עוקבא scolds him for writing to רב הונא as an equal when he did not even know that מרזיחא means a mourner. רבי אבהו and מר זוטרא each bring a פסוק showing that an אבל sits at the head. רבא then rules that food support, the כתובה and a daughter's dowry are collected from the heirs' land only. A new משנה follows: a father leaves money with a שליש to buy a field for his daughter, and she asks that it go to her husband. רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue whether she can override the father. Using a ברייתא and the משנה's last line, the גמרא shows that both agree a קטנה has no say, and that they disagree only about a גדולה during אירוסין. שמואל rules like רבי יוסי, and רב נחמן rules like רבי מאיר. Finally, אילפא claims he can find every ברייתא in a משנה. An old man tests him with a case about a father who gave his sons a weekly שקל, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: מר עוקבא asks what actually happened
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא asks רב ענן to describe the actual incident with רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did the incident itself happen?
steps.whatsHappening: מר עוקבא asks רב ענן to tell him the real story behind his problem with רב הונא. This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before he can judge who was right, מר עוקבא wants the facts. The word גופא points to the actual event itself, not a general summary.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that happened

phrases.english: How did the incident itself happen?
phrases.notes: This is מר עוקבא speaking to רב ענן about his letter to רב הונא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from earlier on the daf about רב ענן and רב הונא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact details of what passed between רב ענן and רב הונא.

steps.title: רב ענן tells the story
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן describes the incident to מר עוקבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Such and such was the incident.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן tells מר עוקבא what happened. The גמרא does not repeat the details here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Such and such' is the גמרא's shorthand. It means he retold the story we already know, including how he opened his letter with 'הונא חברין.'

keyTerms.meaning: Such and such (a shorthand for details)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי וְהָכִי הֲוָה מַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: He said to him: Such and such was the incident.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי וְהָכִי הֲוָה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר עוקבא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ענן relates the full incident.

steps.title: מר עוקבא scolds רב ענן for his casual letter
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא says that someone who does not know what מרזיחא means should not address רב הונא as an equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A man who does not know what a 'מרזיחא' is sends a letter to רב הונא calling him 'הונא, our friend'?!
steps.whatsHappening: מר עוקבא criticizes רב ענן. He was not on רב הונא's level, so calling him 'Huna our friend' was disrespectful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר עוקבא uses a basic word, מרזיחא, as a test. If רב ענן does not know even this, he is not a peer of רב הונא. So רב הונא was right to be offended.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner (explained in the next steps)

phrases.english: He said to him: A man who does not know
what a 'marzeicha' is
sends a letter to Rav Huna
saying 'Huna, our friend'?!
phrases.notes: Writing to someone this way treats him as an equal, which was too casual for a great sage like רב הונא.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבְרָא דְּלָא יָדַע מַאי נִיהוּ מַרְזֵיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: מר עוקבא reacts to the story he just heard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ענן was not on רב הונא's level and should not have addressed him as an equal.

steps.title: What does מרזיחא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word מרזיחא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a 'מרזיחא'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain the word מר עוקבא used. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the whole rebuke depends on this word, the reader also needs to know what it means.

phrases.english: What is a 'marzeicha'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word from מר עוקבא's rebuke.

steps.title: מרזיחא means a mourner
steps.stepSummary: מרזיחא means an אבל, as shown by a פסוק in ירמיהו that calls a house of mourning 'בית מרזח.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A mourner, as it is written: 'For so says ה׳: Do not enter the house of mourning (מרזח)...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that מרזיחא means a mourner and proves it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירמיהו, 'בית מרזח' clearly means a house of mourning, because the פסוק continues with lamenting and grieving. So מרזיחא is an אבל.

phrases.english: A mourner, as it is written:
'For so says ה׳: Do not enter
the house of mourning, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מרזיחא means a mourner, proven from ירמיהו 16:5.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: a mourner sits at the head
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו brings a פסוק in איוב to show that an אבל sits in the place of honor at the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: From where do we know that a mourner sits at the head? As it says: 'I chose their way and sat as head, and dwelt like a king in the army, as one who comforts mourners.'
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the topic of mourners, רבי אבהו gives a source that the אבל sits at the head of the gathering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes someone sitting 'at the head' like a king, and connects this to mourners. רבי אבהו reads it as describing the אבל's seat.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (in a פסוק)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
From where do we know that a mourner sits at the head?
As it says: 'I chose their way and sat as head,
and dwelt like a king in the army,
as one who comforts mourners.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the topic of the אבל just introduced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל sits at the head, learned from איוב 29:25.

steps.title: But the verse speaks of the comforter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'ינחם' means comforting others, so the one sitting at the head is the comforter, not the mourner.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'יְנַחֵם' implies comforting others!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו's proof. As read, the פסוק describes the person who comforts, not the mourner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the one at the head is the comforter, the פסוק teaches nothing about the אבל's seat. The proof seems to fall apart.

phrases.english: 'Yenachem' implies comforting others!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אבהו's proof.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word ינחם is active, so it describes the comforter and not the mourner.

steps.title: The word can be read as 'is comforted'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the letters can be read 'יִנָּחֵם', meaning the one being comforted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is written so that it can be read 'יִנָּחֵם' (is comforted).
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק saves the proof. The written letters also allow a reading that means 'is comforted.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's letters have no vowels, so they can be read two ways. Read as 'יִנָּחֵם', the one sitting at the head is the mourner who is being comforted.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
'Yinachem' (is comforted) is written.
phrases.notes: The same letters, read with different vowels, give 'is comforted.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the word with different vowels
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ינחם means the comforter, so the פסוק is not about the mourner.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read as יִנָּחֵם, the פסוק describes the mourner sitting at the head.

steps.title: מר זוטרא's source from עמוס
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא learns that the אבל sits at the head from 'וסר מרזח סרוחים,' reading מרזח as 'bitter and upset' and סר as 'ruler.'
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: From here: 'And the revelry of those who stretch out shall pass away.' Read it as: one who is bitter and upset becomes the ruler over those who sit.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives a different source for the same rule, using a wordplay on a פסוק in עמוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He splits מרזח into מר (bitter) and זח (upset), which describes the mourner. He reads סר as שר (ruler), so the mourner is 'head' over the visitors who sit with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who stretch out, the people sitting around

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: From here:
'And the revelry of those who stretch out shall pass away.'
One who is bitter and upset
becomes a ruler over those who sit around.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source for רבי אבהו's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mourner sits at the head, learned from עמוס 6:7 by wordplay.
steps.whatToRemember: An אבל sits at the head of those who come to comfort him. רבי אבהו learns it from איוב, and מר זוטרא learns it from עמוס.

steps.title: רבא's ruling: collect only from land
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that food support, the כתובה, and a daughter's dowry are collected from heirs' land only, not from movable property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is that one collects from land and not from movable property, whether for food support, for the כתובה, or for a daughter's dowry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier halachic discussion on the daf and gives the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the question was whether heirs' movable property can be used for these payments. רבא rules that all three are collected only from קרקעות, not from מטלטלין.
steps.whatToRemember: Food support, the כתובה, and a daughter's dowry are collected from land only, never from movable property.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling that closes the long discussion on this daf about what an estate can be used to pay.

phrases.english: Rava said: The halacha is:
from land and not from movable property,
whether for food support or for the ketubah,
or for a daughter's dowry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of mourners and returns to the earlier legal discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Food support, the כתובה and a daughter's dowry are collected only from the heirs' land, not from movable property.

steps.title: A father leaves money with a third party for his daughter
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if a father leaves money with a שליש to buy a field for his daughter, and she asks that it be given to her husband, רבי מאיר says the שליש must follow the father's instructions. רבי יוסי says she controls it, since she could sell a field she owned right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a father leaves money with a third party for his daughter, and she says, 'My husband is trustworthy to me,' the third party must do what he was entrusted to do. That is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יוסי says: if it were just a field and she wanted to sell it, it would be sold right now.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with an argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי. The question is whether a daughter can override her father's instructions about money he set aside for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that the father's instructions bind the שליש. He must buy the field as the father wanted. רבי יוסי reasons that if the field were already hers, she could sell it right away and do what she likes with the money, so the money should already be under her control too.

keyTerms.meaning: One who leaves money with a trusted third party
The third party holding the money
My husband is trustworthy to me

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who leaves money with a third party for his daughter
and she says: My husband is trustworthy to me
the third party should do what was entrusted into his hand
these are the words of Rabbi Meir
Rabbi Yosei says
and if it were only a field
and she wanted to sell it
it would be sold right now
phrases.notes: He means: she could sell her own field, so she can control this money too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the שליש follows the father's instructions. רבי יוסי: the daughter controls the money.

steps.title: This applies only to an adult woman
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits the daughter's control to a גדולה. A קטנה's actions have no legal effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? With an adult woman. But with a minor girl, whatever a minor does means nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a closing line that limits the ruling. It applies only to an adult daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטנה has no legal power to make deals, so her request to redirect the money counts for nothing. The משנה does not say clearly whose view this line belongs to, and the גמרא will soon ask exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said?

phrases.english: In what case are these words said? With an adult woman
but with a minor girl
the action of a minor girl is nothing

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of the משנה to an adult daughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטנה's request has no legal effect.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי מאיר splits between betrothal and marriage
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives רבי מאיר's view in more detail. If the daughter asks after נשואין, she controls the money. If she asks during אירוסין, the שליש follows the father's instructions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One leaves money with a third party for his son-in-law, to buy a field for his daughter, and she says: 'Let it be given to my husband.' If this is from the marriage onward, she has the authority. If it is from the betrothal, the third party must do what he was entrusted to do. That is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out the argument in more detail. This step gives רבי מאיר's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר does not always side with the father. Once she is fully married, the daughter can redirect the money. Only during אירוסין must the שליש stick to the father's instructions.

keyTerms.meaning: The authority is in her hand

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two stages. אירוסין is the first stage of marriage, and נשואין is the full marriage that comes later.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught
one who leaves money with a third party for his son-in-law
to buy with it a field for his daughter
and she says: Let it be given to my husband
if from the marriage
phrases.notes: He means: if she makes this request once she is fully married.

phrases.english: the authority is in her hand
if from the betrothal
the third party should do what was entrusted into his hand
these are the words of Rabbi Meir

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a fuller version of the argument in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: after נשואין she controls the money. During אירוסין the שליש follows the father.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי יוסי splits between adult and minor
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי says a גדולה controls the money at either stage. For a קטנה, at either stage, the שליש follows the father's instructions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: an adult woman, whether from the marriage or from the betrothal, has the authority. A minor girl, whether from the marriage or from the betrothal: the third party must do what he was entrusted to do.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יוסי's side. He makes the split based on her age, not on the stage of marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר divides by stage of marriage. רבי יוסי divides by whether she is an adult or a minor. This different way of dividing the cases sets up the גמרא's next question about where they actually disagree.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר divides by stage (נשואין vs. אירוסין). רבי יוסי divides by age (גדולה vs. קטנה).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: the adult woman

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין וּבֵין מִן הָאֵירוּסִין
phrases.english: whether from the marriage or from the betrothal
the authority is in her hand

phrases.aramaic: קְטַנָּה, בֵּין מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין בֵּין מִן הָאֵירוּסִין
phrases.english: a minor girl, whether from the marriage or from the betrothal
the third party should do what was entrusted into his hand

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יוסי אומר הגדולה בין מן הנשואין ובין מן האירוסין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: a גדולה always controls the money. For a קטנה, the שליש always follows the father.

steps.title: What is the difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in which case רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי actually disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next move. In which real case would רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי rule differently?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rabbis divide the cases in different ways, so it is not obvious where their rulings actually clash. The גמרא wants to find the exact case they disagree on.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the argument laid out in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case where רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי rule differently.

steps.title: Suggested answer: a minor after marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that they disagree about a קטנה after נשואין. רבי מאיר gives her control, and רבי יוסי says that even after marriage only a גדולה has control.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the difference between them is a minor after marriage: רבי מאיר holds she has the authority, and רבי יוסי comes to say that even after marriage, an adult yes, a minor no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer, using the word 'אילימא' ('if you say'). That word warns us the suggestion is about to be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's rule gives any married daughter control, which would seem to include a קטנה. רבי יוסי says a קטנה never has control. So a married minor looks like the case where they clash.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (often a suggestion that will be rejected)
There is a difference between them

phrases.english: If you say: a minor girl from the marriage
is the difference between them
since Rabbi Meir holds the authority is in her hand
and Rabbi Yosei comes to say
that even from the marriage as well
an adult, yes; a minor, no

steps.triggerLanguage: אילימא קטנה מן הנשואין איכא בינייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about a קטנה after נשואין.

steps.title: Challenge from the last line of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion using the משנה's last line, 'a minor's action is nothing.' If רבי יוסי taught that line, it would be extra, because his field argument already shows that only an adult has control.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last clause: 'But with a minor, the action of a minor is nothing.' Who teaches this? If you say רבי יוסי, you already learn it from the first clause, where רבי יוסי said: 'If it were only a field and she wanted to sell it, it would be sold right now.' An adult, who can sell, yes. A minor, who cannot sell, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts attacking the suggested answer. It asks who taught the משנה's line about a minor, and shows it can't simply be רבי יוסי, since that line would add nothing to what he already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's reason is that she could sell her own field. Only a גדולה can make a sale, so his reason already leaves out a קטנה. If the last line were his, it would just repeat what we already know, so the גמרא is pushing toward a different answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone able to make a sale

phrases.english: Say the last clause

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּקְטַנָּה — אֵין מַעֲשֵׂה קְטַנָּה כְּלוּם
phrases.english: But with a minor girl, the action of a minor girl is nothing
Who teaches this?
If you say Rabbi Yosei
you already learn it from the first clause
since Rabbi Yosei said

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא שָׂדֶה וְהִיא רוֹצָה לְמוֹכְרָהּ
phrases.english: and if it were only a field and she wanted to sell it
it would be sold right now
an adult, who is able to sell, yes

phrases.aramaic: קְטַנָּה דְּלָאו בַּת זְבִינֵי הִיא — לָא!
phrases.english: a minor, who is not able to sell, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אימא סיפא אבל בקטנה אין מעשה קטנה כלום
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts challenging the answer suggested in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion in step 16 that רבי מאיר gives a married קטנה control, so that a married minor is where they disagree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last line cannot be רבי יוסי's, because his field argument already excludes a minor and the line would add nothing. So it must be רבי מאיר's, which means רבי מאיר also gives a קטנה no control, contradicting step 16 (finished in step 18).

steps.title: The last line of the משנה belongs to רבי מאיר, with missing words filled in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the last line, 'a minor's action is nothing,' is רבי מאיר's. It reads the משנה as missing words and fills them in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is רבי מאיר, and the משנה is missing words. It means: the שליש does what was entrusted to him. When is that said? During אירוסין. But after נשואין, she has the authority. When is that said? With a גדולה. But with a קטנה, a minor's action is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 17. It says the line 'a minor's action is nothing' was never רבי יוסי's at all. It is the end of רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי said that line, it would be extra, since his field argument already limits control to an adult. So the גמרא gives the line to רבי מאיר and rebuilds the משנה with missing words. Now רבי מאיר says that even after נשואין, only a גדולה gets control. A קטנה never does.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words (and we fill them in)
And this is what it teaches
A third party who holds money for others
When is this said? (a formula that limits a rule)
The authority is in her hands

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי מאיר gives a קטנה control after נשואין. That was the suggestion in step 16, and this step drops it. In the rebuilt משנה, רבי מאיר also says a קטנה's action means nothing.

phrases.english: Rather, it is Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: The last line of the משנה, 'a minor's action is nothing,' belongs to רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: and it is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
The third party should do what was entrusted into his hand.
When is this said? From the betrothal.
But from the marriage, the authority is in her hand.
When is this said? With an adult woman.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּקְטַנָּה — אֵין מַעֲשֵׂה קְטַנָּה כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: But with a minor, a minor's action is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, וְחַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the extra-words challenge of step 17 by giving the משנה's last line to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reattribution of a clause plus filling in missing words (חסורי מיחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last line was רבי יוסי's, and רבי מאיר gave a קטנה control after נשואין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The last line is רבי מאיר's. According to him, only a גדולה after נשואין has control, and a קטנה never does.

steps.title: The real disagreement: an adult woman during betrothal
steps.stepSummary: Since both agree a קטנה has no control, the גמרא concludes that the difference is a גדולה during אירוסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between them is an adult woman during אירוסין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a new answer to the question from step 15: where do רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי disagree? The answer is an adult woman who is only engaged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages now agree that a קטנה has no control and that a גדולה after נשואין has control. The only case left is a גדולה during אירוסין. There רבי מאיר says the שליש follows the father, and רבי יוסי says she controls the money.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.whatToRemember: Final map: a קטנה never has control (both agree). A גדולה after נשואין has control (both agree). A גדולה during אירוסין is the מחלוקת: רבי מאיר says no, רבי יוסי says yes.

phrases.english: Rather, an adult woman from the betrothal
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גְּדוֹלָה מִן הָאֵירוּסִין אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the step 18 reading means for the step 15 question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In which case do רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי disagree (step 15)?

steps.title: אמוראים disagree about whom the הלכה follows
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules like רבי יוסי, and רב נחמן rules like רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. רבא said in the name of רב נחמן, the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the מחלוקת is clear, the גמרא reports that later אמוראים also disagree about which view is the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their disagreement is about the case found in step 19, a גדולה during אירוסין. Following שמואל, she controls the money. Following רב נחמן, the שליש follows the father's instructions until נשואין.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute among אמוראים)

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a תנאים dispute into a practical question: who decides about money set aside for an engaged adult woman.

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Yosei.
Rava said that Rav Nachman said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the מחלוקת defined in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: הלכה like רבי יוסי. רב נחמן: הלכה like רבי מאיר.

steps.title: אילפא hangs from a ship's mast and makes a bold challenge
steps.stepSummary: אילפא hangs from a ship's mast. He declares that if anyone brings him a teaching from the school of רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא and he cannot find it in a משנה, he will fall and drown.
steps.simpleTranslation: אילפא hung himself from the mast of a ship and said: If someone comes and tells me a teaching of the school of רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא, and I cannot resolve it from a משנה, I will fall from the mast and drown.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. אילפא makes a dramatic public claim that every ברייתא can be found in the משנה, which sets up the test in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא collected ברייתות, which are teachings left out of the משנה. אילפא claims the משנה already contains all of them if you read it closely. The text here does not say why he did this. It only shows how sure he was.

keyTerms.meaning: I resolve / I show the answer

phrases.english: Ilfa hung himself
from the mast of a ship,
he said: If there is someone who comes and tells me

phrases.aramaic: מִילְּתָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
phrases.english: a teaching of the school of Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Oshaya,
and I do not resolve it from a Mishnah,
I will fall from the mast and drown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the הלכה ruling closed the שליש discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אילפא claims every ברייתא of רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא can be found in a משנה.

steps.title: An old man tests אילפא with a case about giving money to sons
steps.stepSummary: An old man teaches a ברייתא: a man tells the court to give his sons a שקל each week. The ruling depends on his exact wording and on whether he named later heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: An old man came and taught him: If someone says 'give my sons a שקל each week,' and they need a סלע, we give them a סלע. If he said 'give them only a שקל,' we give only a שקל. If he said 'if they die, others will inherit in their place,' then whether he said 'give' or 'don't give,' we give them only a שקל.
steps.whatsHappening: The old man takes up אילפא's challenge and quotes a ברייתא. He does not say the question out loud, but the test is clear: show where this is in a משנה. This sets up the next step, where אילפא must answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the plain case, the father's 'שקל' is taken as a rough amount, so the sons get more if they need it. 'Only a שקל' is a clear limit. Once he names other heirs, the money must be saved for them, so even plain wording is held to a שקל.

keyTerms.meaning: Others will inherit in their place

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the sons are punished in the last case. The father wants the estate kept whole for the later heirs, so the court gives only exactly what he said.

phrases.english: A certain old man came and taught him:
One who says, 'Give a shekel to my sons each week,'
and it is fitting to give them a sela,
we give them a sela.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר ״אַל תִּתְּנוּ לָהֶם אֶלָּא שֶׁקֶל״ —
phrases.english: And if he said, 'Give them only a shekel,'
we give them only a shekel.
And if he said, 'If they die,
others will inherit in their place,'
whether he said 'give' or whether he said 'don't give,'
we give them only a shekel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes up אילפא's challenge by presenting a ברייתא for him to trace to a משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father's 'שקל' is loose wording unless he says 'only a שקל' or names later heirs. In those cases the court gives exactly a שקל.

steps.title: אילפא asks whose opinion the teaching follows
steps.stepSummary: אילפא responds to the old man's ברייתא by asking which תנא it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: אילפא said to him: Whose opinion is this ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: אילפא starts answering the old man's test by asking which תנא the ברייתא follows. This line sets up the next move, where the author will be named.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To find a ברייתא inside a משנה, אילפא first needs to know which תנא's way of thinking it follows. Once the author is known, he can point to a משנה that holds the same idea. So this question is the first step in keeping his promise.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? A standard question asking which תנא a teaching follows
The אמורא who claimed he could find every ברייתא of רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא in a משנה
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה itself

phrases.english: He said to him: Whose opinion is this?
phrases.notes: אילפא is speaking to the old man who just taught the ברייתא about the weekly שקל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אילפא responds to the old man's test from Step 22 by first asking who the ברייתא's author is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the ברייתא about the weekly שקל follows, so it can be matched to a משנה.
